title: Choosing Between Azure VM and App Service
description: Decide between IaaS (VMs) and PaaS (App Service) for hosting a web application.

data.text: You need to host a .NET 8 web API that connects to Azure SQL Database. The team wants minimal infrastructure management, automatic patching, and built-in CI/CD. Should you use Azure VMs or App Service?

Choose **Azure App Service** for web applications and APIs. It provides automatic OS patching, built-in load balancing, deployment slots, and integration with Azure DevOps. Use VMs only when you need full OS control.

data.title: Azure CLI - Create App Service Plan and Web App
data.code:
# Create App Service Plan
az appservice plan create \
  --name 'myAppPlan' \
  --resource-group 'rg-ecommerce' \
  --sku 'P1V3' \
  --number-of-workers 1

# Create Web App
az webapp create \
  --name 'my-ecommerce-api' \
  --resource-group 'rg-ecommerce' \
  --plan 'myAppPlan' \
  --runtime 'DOTNETCORE:8.0'

data.text: **App Service** is PaaS: Azure manages the OS, patching, and infrastructure. **VMs** are IaaS: you manage everything. For web apps, App Service reduces operational overhead by ~70% compared to VMs.

cards.title: Azure App Service
cards.description: Fully managed PaaS for web apps

data.title: Decision Guide
data.text: Use **App Service** for web apps and APIs. Use **AKS** for complex microservices. Use **VMs** only when you need custom OS configuration or are migrating legacy applications.
